easy.question: When does the event in the verse occur?
answers: After Moses' death
Before Moses' death
During David's reign
easy.explanation: The opening 'Now after the death of Moses...' indicates it happens after Moses has died.

easy.question: Who is called 'the servant of the LORD' in the verse?
answers: Joshua
Moses
Nun
easy.explanation: The verse reads 'the death of Moses the servant of the LORD' — the phrase refers to Moses.

easy.question: To whom does the LORD speak in the verse?
answers: To the priests
To Moses
To Joshua the son of Nun
easy.explanation: The verse says 'the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun' — it is addressed to Joshua.

medium.question: What is Joshua's role as written in the verse?
answers: Judge over the people
Moses' minister/attendant
A lone prophet
medium.explanation: The verse calls him 'Moses' minister' — i.e., Moses' assistant.

medium.question: Context: the phrase 'Moses' minister' — what does it mean here?
answers: Moses' direct successor as leader
Someone unrelated to Moses
An assistant/servant of Moses
medium.explanation: 'Minister' here means an assistant or attendant; the context shows he served alongside Moses.

medium.question: Why does the LORD address Joshua in this verse?
answers: Because Moses is dead
Because Joshua seized power by force
Because the people elected him
medium.explanation: The verse begins 'Moses my servant is dead' — that is the reason God speaks to a new leader.

challenge.question: What logical conclusion follows from the sequence 'Moses died' then 'the LORD spoke to Joshua'?
answers: That God stopped speaking to the people
That the people no longer needed a leader
A transfer of authority and that Moses' successor was chosen
challenge.explanation: After Moses' death the LORD speaks to Joshua — this implies continuity and transfer of authority.

challenge.question: What does the epithet 'son of Nun' in 'Joshua son of Nun' indicate?
answers: Identification of his father and family
A geographic description of birthplace
A royal or honorary title
challenge.explanation: In biblical names 'son of ...' normally identifies the father's name or lineage.

challenge.question: Which phrase in the verse shows that God's address is directed personally to Joshua?
answers: 'the servant of the LORD'
'the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun'
'Now after the death of Moses'
challenge.explanation: The phrase 'the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun' is a direct address from God to Joshua.

answers: That God stopped speaking to the people
That the people no longer needed a leader

answers: 'the servant of the LORD'
'the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun'
'Now after the death of Moses'
questions.explanation: The phrase 'the LORD spake unto Joshua the son of Nun' is a direct address from God to Joshua.

easy.question: Who died at the start of this passage?
answers: Moses
Joshua
Aaron
easy.explanation: The passage begins 'Moses my servant is dead' — Moses has died.

easy.question: What does the LORD command Joshua to do in verse 2?
answers: Go down to Egypt
Cross this Jordan into the land
Return to the wilderness
easy.explanation: He is told 'Arise, go over this Jordan' — to cross into the land.

easy.question: Who is to cross the Jordan according to the verse?
answers: Joshua alone
Only the people without their leader
You and all this people
easy.explanation: The command is 'thou, and all this people' — both Joshua and the people are to cross.

medium.question: What does the promise in verse 3 'Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread' mean?
answers: Land will be given only after negotiations
Places they set foot on will be given to them
The wilderness is excluded from the promise
medium.explanation: It states that every place they tread will be given — possession corresponds to places they occupy.

medium.question: Context: the phrase 'shall be your coast' — what does 'coast' mean here?
answers: Their private dwelling place (house)
A path or road
The territorial boundary assigned to you
medium.explanation: 'Coast' here means territory or boundary; the following list of borders shows it refers to territorial limits.

medium.question: Which of the following is included in the borders the LORD sets in verse 4?
answers: The great sea toward the going down of the sun
The Nile River
The Himalayas
medium.explanation: Verse 4 mentions 'the great sea toward the going down of the sun' — i.e., the western sea is included.

challenge.question: How should 'Every place ... which the sole of your foot shall tread upon I have given unto you' be understood regarding how the land is obtained?
answers: As immediate possession of all the land without struggle
As a purely spiritual promise
As a step-by-step promise — they will possess areas as they set foot on them
challenge.explanation: The wording indicates lands are given corresponding to places they occupy — gradual acquisition through possession.

challenge.question: What river is 'the river Euphrates' mentioned in verse 4?
answers: The Euphrates River
The Jordan River
The Nile River
challenge.explanation: 'The river Euphrates' is the Euphrates, cited as a major eastern boundary.

challenge.question: Who is the speaker when the phrase 'which I do give unto them' appears in verse 3?
answers: Moses speaking second-hand
The LORD speaking to Joshua and granting the land
Joshua speaking to the people
challenge.explanation: The LORD is speaking to Joshua in the passage, so 'I do give' is God declaring the gift of the land.

questions.question: How should 'Every place ... which the sole of your foot shall tread upon I have given unto you' be understood regarding how the land is obtained?

As a step-by-step promise — they will possess areas as they set foot on them

answers: Moses speaking second-hand

Joshua speaking to the people
questions.explanation: The LORD is speaking to Joshua in the passage, so 'I do give' is God declaring the gift of the land.

easy.question: What is the plain meaning of 'There shall not any man be able to stand before thee' in this verse?
answers: No one will stand against you or prevail over you
Everyone will stand beside you
No one will teach you
easy.explanation: The phrase means no person will oppose or successfully withstand you.

easy.question: What additional promise is given to Joshua in the verse besides the command?
answers: That God will be with him as He was with Moses
That he will gain many possessions
That he will have superhuman strength
easy.explanation: The verse promises 'as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee' — God will accompany Joshua.

easy.question: Who is mentioned as the example of God's past relationship?
answers: Aaron
Moses
David
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly references Moses.

medium.question: Why does the verse say 'as I was with Moses' when God speaks to Joshua?
answers: To reassure Joshua and promise the same divine accompaniment
To say Joshua will become Moses' identical replacement in appearance and traits
To compare the sins of Moses and Joshua
medium.explanation: Mentioning Moses reassures Joshua of continued divine support and continuity.

medium.question: Context: the phrase 'I will not fail thee' — what does 'fail thee' mean in 'I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee'?
answers: To give up hope in you
To stop supporting or to abandon you
To punish you
medium.explanation: Here 'fail thee' means to cease supporting or to abandon; the promise is ongoing support, not abandonment.

medium.question: What does the phrase 'all the days of thy life' mean in this context?
answers: Throughout Joshua's lifetime
Only while Joshua's administration lasts
Only for a short limited time
medium.explanation: It refers to the entire span of Joshua's life — the promise applies during his life.

challenge.question: How should the promise 'There shall not any man be able to stand before thee' be understood practically?
answers: That no rival will contest Joshua's authority
That there will be no military enemies in the land at all
That everyone will gather physically before Joshua
challenge.explanation: Practically it grants leadership authority — no competitor will stand against him; it does not mean absolute absence of military opposition.

challenge.question: Why is the mention of Moses historically and politically important in this verse?
answers: To show continuity of leadership and that the people should accept Joshua as they accepted Moses
To say Joshua will be greater than Moses in every respect
To erase Moses' memory
challenge.explanation: Mentioning Moses links the leadership periods and legitimizes Joshua by promising the same divine accompaniment.

challenge.question: What is the stylistic effect of the repetition 'I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee'?
answers: It strengthens the promise by using parallel negation
It adds a condition linking the promises
It expresses doubt about the promise
challenge.explanation: The paired negatives intensify and emphasize the assurance of God's presence.

easy.question: What repeated command appears in these verses?
answers: Be strong and of a good courage
Keep the law
Go and be honored
easy.explanation: 'Be strong and of a good courage' is repeated as encouragement to Joshua.

easy.question: Who promises to be with Joshua 'whithersoever thou goest'?
answers: The people
The LORD thy God
Moses
easy.explanation: Verse 9 states 'for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest'.

easy.question: What is Joshua charged to do in verse 6?
answers: Build a sanctuary
Write a book
Divide the land among the people as an inheritance
easy.explanation: He is told to divide the people the land which the LORD swore to give to their fathers.

medium.question: Context: 'turn not from it to the right hand or to the left' — what does 'turn not from it' mean?
answers: To stray or deviate from it
To guard it closely
To hurry
medium.explanation: It means do not stray or deviate from the law; don't shift to the right or left.

medium.question: Why does the verse command that 'this book of the law' not depart from your mouth and be meditated on day and night?
answers: So you may keep and do all that is written
To memorize the tribe names
To preserve local customs
medium.explanation: Continuous meditation ensures obedience to all that is written and leads to success.

medium.question: According to verse 7, whose command about the law is Joshua to observe?
answers: The people
Moses my servant
Joshua himself
medium.explanation: The verse attributes the law to 'Moses my servant' — Joshua should follow Moses' instructions.

challenge.question: What is the practical meaning of the repeated command 'Be strong and of a good courage'?
answers: To encourage Joshua and reinforce his leadership
A warning that the people will not obey
A technical order to build a camp
challenge.explanation: Repetition emphasizes divine encouragement and the need for courage in leadership during conquest.

challenge.question: According to verse 8, what result follows if Joshua keeps and does the law?
answers: You will prosper and afterward succeed
You will gain understanding before success
Nothing special will happen
challenge.explanation: Verse links obedience with prospering and having success — obedience leads to prosperity and success.

challenge.question: What does 'the land' refer to in verse 6 in the historical-biblical context?
answers: The desert region only
The land of Egypt
The land of Canaan promised to the fathers
challenge.explanation: In context 'the land' refers to Canaan, the promised land given to the patriarchs.

questions.explanation: Repetition emphasizes divine encouragement and the need for courage in leadership during conquest.

answers: The desert region only
The land of Egypt
The land of Canaan promised to the fathers
questions.explanation: In context 'the land' refers to Canaan, the promised land given to the patriarchs.

easy.question: What did Joshua command the officers of the people to do?
answers: Pass through the camp and command the people
Recruit mercenaries
Build an altar
easy.explanation: He told the officers to pass through the camp and give the command to the people.

easy.question: What were the people instructed to prepare?
answers: Sharpen their swords
Victuals (provisions) for the journey
Dig trenches
easy.explanation: 'Prepare you victuals' means prepare food and supplies for the upcoming crossing.

easy.question: How many days in advance were they told to be ready before crossing the Jordan?
answers: One day
A week
Three days
easy.explanation: The officers were told 'within three days ye shall pass over this Jordan' — three days' notice.

medium.question: Why did Joshua command preparation of victuals before crossing?
answers: So they would be ready for the journey and entry into the land
To hold a ceremony in the camp
To guard the camp as they returned
medium.explanation: Provisions were needed for the march and entry into the promised land.

medium.question: What does the word 'victuals' mean in the phrase 'Prepare you victuals'?
answers: Weapons and armor
Food and supplies for a journey
Jewelry and ornaments
medium.explanation: 'Victuals' refers to food and provisions for travel.

medium.question: Who gives them the land according to the verse?
answers: The leaders of the people
They will take it by their own effort
The LORD your God
medium.explanation: The verse states the land is given by 'the LORD your God'.

challenge.question: What does the command 'Pass through the host' imply about how the message is to be delivered?
answers: That officers should go among the units and inform each group orderly
To evict the whole camp and hide the message
To tell only the leaders secretly
challenge.explanation: It implies moving through the camp to notify all soldiers and units in an orderly manner.

challenge.question: Which river is meant by 'this Jordan' when they are told to pass over it?
answers: The Nile
The Jordan
The Euphrates
challenge.explanation: The passage refers to the Jordan River, which they must cross to enter the land.

challenge.question: What practical meaning does 'to possess the land' have in this verse?
answers: To levy taxes on current inhabitants
To build a new capital city
To take control of the land and receive it as an inheritance
challenge.explanation: 'To possess the land' means to take control of and settle the land as their inheritance.

questions.question: What does the command 'Pass through the host' imply about how the message is to be delivered?
answers: That officers should go among the units and inform each group orderly
To evict the whole camp and hide the message
To tell only the leaders secretly
questions.explanation: It implies moving through the camp to notify all soldiers and units in an orderly manner.

answers: The Nile
The Jordan

questions.explanation: The passage refers to the Jordan River, which they must cross to enter the land.

answers: To levy taxes on current inhabitants

questions.explanation: 'To possess the land' means to take control of and settle the land as their inheritance.

easy.question: To whom did Joshua speak in these verses?
answers: To Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh
To all Israel everywhere
To the priests only
easy.explanation: The address is made to the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

easy.question: What was Joshua telling them to remember in verse 13?
answers: To always be ready for war
That Moses commanded and the LORD gave them rest and the land
To leave the land and return to the wilderness
easy.explanation: He reminded them of Moses' command that the LORD had given them rest and the land.

easy.question: Where would their wives, children and cattle remain according to verse 14?
answers: In Canaan west of the Jordan
With them when they went into battle
In the land on this side of the Jordan that Moses gave them
easy.explanation: They would remain in the land Moses gave them on the east side of the Jordan.

medium.question: What was expected of the armed men during battle according to these verses?
answers: To cross the next day and help their brethren valiantly
To scout the camp and report to leaders
To stay behind and protect their families
medium.explanation: They were to pass before their brethren armed and help them in battle.

medium.question: Context: the phrase 'pass before your brethren armed' — what does 'armed' mean?
answers: Divided into two units
Equipped and ready for battle
Weak and unarmed
medium.explanation: Here 'armed' means equipped and prepared for combat, as they were to go before their brethren and assist.

medium.question: When may these tribes return to their possession across the Jordan according to verse 15?
answers: Immediately after the months decide to return
Before the wars in the west begin
After the LORD gives their brethren rest and they also possess the land
medium.explanation: They will return after the LORD grants their brethren rest and they have possessed the land.

challenge.question: What does 'until the LORD have given your brethren rest' mean in context?
answers: Until God grants rest to their brethren and they receive their inheritance
Until their men choose to return home for personal reasons
Until every enemy has been driven out completely
challenge.explanation: It means they must help until the LORD enables their brethren to settle and take possession.

challenge.question: Where is the inheritance located for the families that remained, described as 'toward the sunrising'?
answers: In an unknown region without direction
East of the Jordan — 'toward the rising of the sun'
On the Mediterranean coast
challenge.explanation: 'Toward the sunrising' indicates the eastern side of the Jordan (the east).

challenge.question: What follows from the phrase 'and ye shall return and possess the land which Moses gave you' about the arrangement?
answers: They will give up their inheritance forever
Their inheritance will be reassigned after a census
After their brethren inherit in the west, they will return to their eastern allotments as Moses gave them
challenge.explanation: They are to resume their eastern inheritance once their brethren have settled the west.

answers: Until God grants rest to their brethren and they receive their inheritance

Until every enemy has been driven out completely
questions.explanation: It means they must help until the LORD enables their brethren to settle and take possession.

paragraphs.title: The People Pledge and Are Loyal

easy.question: What do the people say to Joshua in verse 16?
answers: We will do all that you command and go wherever you send us
We will refrain from war in your land
We will leave the wilderness
easy.explanation: They promise obedience and to go wherever Joshua sends them.

easy.question: How do the people compare their attitude toward Joshua to their attitude toward Moses in verse 17?
answers: They will only obey if Joshua teaches them new sections
They will obey him just as they obeyed Moses
They will obey only some of his commands
easy.explanation: They declare they will hearken to Joshua as they hearkened to Moses.

easy.question: What is the penalty for anyone who rebels against Joshua's command in verse 18?
answers: A warning only
Exile from the camp
Death
easy.explanation: The verse states that whoever disobeys will be put to death.

medium.question: Why do the people add 'Only the LORD your God be with thee' in verse 17?
answers: Because they are willing to obey but see Joshua's success depends on God's presence
Because they do not believe Joshua at all
Because they want God punished instead of Joshua
medium.explanation: They pledge obedience but emphasize Joshua's success depends on the LORD being with him as He was with Moses.

medium.question: Context: the phrase 'Whosoever shall rebel against thy commandment' — what does 'rebel' mean?
answers: To deny the orders and disobey
To speak quietly without action
To comply fully
medium.explanation: Here 'rebel' means to actively disobey or resist Joshua's commands.

medium.question: What special promise does the people give in verse 16 regarding movement and following Joshua?
answers: That they will teach Joshua to teach others
That they will assist him only in military tasks
That they will go wherever Joshua sends them
medium.explanation: They explicitly commit to go to all places Joshua sends them.

challenge.question: Why does the chapter end with the exhortation 'Be strong and courageous' to Joshua?
answers: To encourage him to meet the leadership responsibilities and the conquest ahead
To warn him not to rely on the LORD
To tell him he may retire if he wishes
challenge.explanation: The exhortation encourages Joshua as he assumes great responsibility and faces the challenge of conquest.

challenge.question: What is the grammatical function of 'only' in 'only the LORD thy God be with thee' (verse 17)?
answers: It emphasizes the king over God
It expresses a condition/limitation on their commitment
It replaces 'also' to add another action
challenge.explanation: 'Only' introduces a limitation or condition: they will obey provided the LORD is with Joshua.

challenge.question: Who are the speakers making these pledges in verses 16–18?
answers: Canaanite tribes trying to deceive Joshua
Joshua's close servants only
The people of Israel who followed Moses and now stand under Joshua's leadership
challenge.explanation: The speakers are the Israelites who promise obedience to Joshua as they did to Moses.

questions.question: Why does the chapter end with the exhortation 'Be strong and courageous' to Joshua?
answers: To encourage him to meet the leadership responsibilities and the conquest ahead
To warn him not to rely on the LORD
To tell him he may retire if he wishes
questions.explanation: The exhortation encourages Joshua as he assumes great responsibility and faces the challenge of conquest.
